description: On a project under exclusive routing with the guard enforcing, `focus open` registers a focus cycle as a quick task, the installed guard lets a source write through while it is open, `focus close` records it in state.md and the batch, and the same write is denied once it is closed.
why: Focus–phase integration (spec D2): a focus run used to be invisible to PAN, so exclusive routing would deny its own edits. A cycle is now a quick-task record that the guard counts as work in flight with no guard change. Unit tests prove it against the source hook; this proves it against the packed install, and the control proves the allow comes from the open cycle.

steps.why: The installed engine registers the batch as quick task 1, before any edit.
An open focus cycle is work in flight: the installed guard lets the write to src/a.js through under exclusive routing and enforce.
The close measures the tests again (1 passing before and after) and derives the status: one item failed, so the cycle is partial. It writes the summary, the batch results and the state row.
state.md gains a Quick Tasks row that links the cycle directory.
The batch records each item's result under its own key.
With the cycle closed nothing is in flight: the same write is denied.

controls.why: Without the registered cycle nothing is in flight, so the first guard step must see a deny: the allow comes from the open cycle, not from the guard being off.
